correctness.rationale: The beta integral gives the stated norms with total mass one, and analytic and anti-analytic nonconstant monomials have zero mixed inner product. This yields twice the real part of the binomial kernel minus one, on its disk branch. For s=r exp(iθ), differentiation gives the negative sine in RESULT.md lines 44–52. The argument ψ is strictly concave on (0,π); its tangent at zero bounds it by r(π−θ)/(1+r), putting the sine argument strictly between 0 and π when βr≤1. This verifies the unique angular minimum at the antipode. Strict convexity gives β(2^(1/β)−1)<1 for β>1, and the antipodal value crosses zero exactly at that radius. Above it and below 1/β the opposite endpoint signs and strict monotonicity give exactly one zero on each semicircle; these are scalar products, not isolated points in the bidisk. At the first zero the radial derivative is −β/(1+ρ) and the coefficient of the squared angular displacement is βρ(1−βρ)/(2(1+ρ)^2). Even real analyticity and the implicit function theorem in the squared displacement yield the given coefficient and O((r−ρ)^(3/2)) remainder. For 0<β≤1 the same circle estimate gives strict positivity for every r<1, in the coefficient-defined continuation only.
